limits: trust boundary: every rule holds only against a caller that reaches the store through the engine; a process that can write the store folder can append records itself, and one that can start its own engine on it can ignore every check

in this demo the agent, the store folder and the human cosign key belong to one OS user: it shows the cosign mechanism, not the separation that "the agent cannot self-cosign" needs (key outside the agent's reach AND no agent write access to the store folder or way to run another engine on it)
the opener of a key is trusted for its tenant, original and facts; disasters 2 and 3 are blocked relative to those values; the tenant field is not authenticated
the read airlock checks only the top-level tenant_id of the rows passed to it and returns parsed copies of the checked bytes
a lease is bound to (request id, tenant, key); only handlers that opened a lease are covered
pins: the engine pins the refund binary and (through its compiled-in helper) the checker model; the store pins the SHA-256 of the Node binary at init; a file swapped after its check is not detected
Stripe and PayPal are LOCAL FAKE in-process stand-ins; SIGKILL is not a power loss; end_to_end=false

rustc 1.92.0, LLVM and the Rust standard library; Node 24.3.0 and node:crypto (Ed25519); the Dafny 4.11.0 compiler and JavaScript runtime; bignumber.js 9.3.1 loaded from the pinned node_modules (package-lock.json; checked by scripts/javascript_env.py, not by the model pin); Python 3.10.11.
The JSON-to-Dafny generator of diff_policy.py (owner decision, Goal 20 plan line 8).

Trust boundary (review finding 1): every rule holds only against a caller that reaches the store THROUGH the engine. A process that can write the store folder can append records itself, and one that can start its own engine build on the store can ignore every check. "The agent cannot self-cosign" needs the private key out of the agent's reach AND no agent write access to the store folder and no way for the agent to run another engine on it. In the demo all three belong to one OS user: it shows the mechanism only.
The opener of a key is trusted (review finding 6): the money caps rest on the original amount and the facts that the opener chooses; the tenant field is not authenticated.
The read airlock checks only the TOP-LEVEL tenant_id of the rows passed to it (review finding 10); a nested row of another tenant passes. It sees only the rows passed to it.

What pins what: the engine embeds the two Node helpers (include_str!, no helper file is read at run time) and pins the refund binary (SHA-256 b8ed5ec2...7bb8); the store pins the SHA-256 of the Node binary in its genesis record at init; booking_check.cjs pins the compiled model (e705ec49...85f4); the genesis record pins the policy files (FNV-1a-128, not cryptographic); bin/forge-airlock re-checks its private refund copy; nothing pins the engine binary itself or bignumber.js. A file swapped between its hash and its exec is not detected. The test seams AIRLOCK_TEST_HELPERS and AIRLOCK_TEST_UNPINNED_BINARY exist only in the kill_points build.

Cosign: an agent that runs as the same OS user as the key owner can read a 0600 key file; "the agent cannot self-cosign" holds only when the private key is outside its reach (and see the trust boundary above). Weak (small-order or non-canonical) Ed25519 keys and signature R values are refused.

FNV-1a-128 collisions can be computed (review finding 11): the compare-and-swap is a concurrency control, not a boundary against an attacker. A restore of the WAL and the ratchet together is not detected.
